name: Sabin Boys
description: Sabin Boys were an independent street gang active in Chicago's Ukrainian Village neighborhood from the mid-1960s through at least the early 1970s. The name likely derives from Sabin Elementary School in the area. They were one of several local gangs — alongside the Haddon Boys, UK's, and Dragons — who at times allied with the Spanish Lords against the Chi-West gang in conflicts centered around the Chopin school area (Iowa St. and Rice St.).
